info.title: corvus
info.description: MCP server and command line for reverse engineering and security analysis of .NET assemblies and native PE, ELF and Mach-O binaries: decompile, search, compare builds, patch and save. By default nothing is executed.

commands.name: batch
commands.description:
Read one file with fixed read-only steps (summary, container, strings,
yara) into one corvus.batch/1 document. --rules <file|folder>, --time-limit S,
--limit containerFiles=N, --limit strings=N, --limit yaraMatches=N.

commands.name: call
commands.description:
The same. Values: name=value (typed by the parameter), name:=<json>, name=@file,
name=@- (stdin); or --args '<json object>' (also --json '{...}'), --args-file F|-.
--load PATH preloads (repeatable); any server option applies (docs/configuration.md).
--json          print {tool, isError, text, structured, error}
--structured    print only the structured content

commands.name: completion
commands.description: A completion script for bash, zsh or pwsh.

commands.name: config
commands.description:
Print the configuration to add by hand (for clients not listed).
--dev-reload DIR  the relay's configuration (see install)

commands.name: describe
commands.description: A tool's or prompt's description, parameters and an example (help <name> too).

commands.name: ida-script
commands.description:
Write corvus_connect.py and its worker for IDA's File > Script file; it serves
the open database to Corvus when CORVUS_IDA_CONNECT=1.
Tool exit codes: 0 success, 1 tool error, 2 usage or invalid_argument, 3 engine missing or unsupported,
124 timeout, 130 cancelled (Ctrl+C).

commands.name: install
commands.description:
Register the server with MCP clients and check that it starts.
Existing registrations are refreshed. New detected clients are added after one
confirmation (Enter = yes); without a terminal, only with --yes (CORVUS_YES=1)
or --all-detected.
--client X      only these clients (repeatable or comma-separated), detected or not
--dry-run       print the plan and write nothing (--check also runs the server check)
--json          print the plan and result as JSON (needs --yes to add new clients)
--strict        write nothing when any client's file cannot be read
--no-check      skip the server check
--command PATH  register this program instead of the running one
--dev-reload DIR  development: register the relay, which runs the server
published in DIR (./publish.ps1) and follows each new publish
--skill         also write the agent skill for clients that read skills
(install and update keep written skills current)
--enable        turn on an entry the client has turned off; otherwise it stays off
--set S         add a security switch to every entry, e.g. --set allow-live-attach
--unset S       remove it (docs/configuration.md lists the switches)
--project DIR   with --set/--unset: only this folder's Claude Code entry,
made from the global one when the folder has none
--with-live     install the tested Frida into a private Python environment now
and --set live-install-frida (sessions use it)
uninstall [client...] Remove the registration from every client, or the named ones, and the skill
folders install wrote. Without names it also deletes an installed copy's program
files (--keep-files keeps them). Data is kept; --purge-data deletes it too.
--dry-run and --json as for install.

commands.name: prompts
commands.description: List the prompts; prompt <name> [name=value ...] prints one, ready to pipe.

arguments.name: PLAN_PATCH
arguments.description:
Find the right patch point for a behaviour change, preview it, apply it and save a patched copy.
goal, assembly?

arguments.name: FIND_FEATURE
arguments.description:
Locate the code that implements a behaviour, starting from strings, names and constants.
feature, assembly?

arguments.name: ANALYZE_ASSEMBLY
arguments.description:
Load an assembly or application folder and produce an architecture overview.
path, focus?

arguments.name: GUIDE
arguments.description:
The guidance on one area; without a topic, the core and the topic list.
topic?

arguments.name: PATCH_NATIVE
arguments.description:
Find the instruction that decides a behaviour, preview and apply a patch, and save a patched copy.
image, goal

arguments.name: EXPLAIN_TYPE
arguments.description:
Explain what a type does, how it is used, and its important members.
type, assembly?

arguments.name: INVESTIGATE_FEATURE
arguments.description:
From a behaviour the user describes to the code behind it, with recorded evidence and listed unkn...
behaviour, target?, evidencePath?

arguments.name: ANALYZE_NATIVE
arguments.description: Load a native file and produce an overview: build, hardening, imports and main code areas.

arguments.name: GETTING_STARTED
arguments.description: How this server works and a first session on a file of your choice.

arguments.name: FIND_API_USAGE
arguments.description:
Every call site of an imported function and what the callers pass and do with the result.
image, api
check_reimplementation Emulate a native function on chosen inputs and compare with the expected outputs.
image, function, computes, cases?

arguments.name: COMPARE_BUILDS
arguments.description:
What changed between two builds, and carry existing work to the new one.
oldPath, newPath, focus?

arguments.name: MAP_NATIVE_ADDRESS
arguments.description:
Identify the managed method behind a native address in an AOT build, from IDA, Ghidra or a crash...
address, dummyDllFolder?

arguments.name: TRACE_NATIVE_FEATURE
arguments.description:
Find the native code behind a behaviour, from strings, APIs and constants to the deciding function.
feature, image
15 prompts. Render one: corvus prompt <name> name=value ...

commands.name: resources
commands.description: List resources and templates; read <uri> prints one.

commands.name: rules
commands.description:
Installed and known YARA rule packs; rules fetch <pack> downloads one (SHA-256 checked)
for search_container kind=yara query=pack:<name>.

commands.name: status
commands.description:
Read-only check: starts each client's registered command with its args and env,
and checks this build's server and catalog digest, the engines and installed skills.
--client X      only these clients (fails only for them)
--engine E      only ida, python, ghidra or all (--deep also starts IDA's worker)
--target PATH   what the file is and which engines read it
--json          the report as JSON

commands.name: tools
commands.description: List the tools by toolset (--json for a table).

commands.name: add_search_directory
commands.description: edit         Add a folder where referenced assemblies that are not loaded are resolved.

commands.name: list_assemblies
commands.description: read-only    Loaded assemblies and native images with ids, versions, flags and unsaved edits, plus the referen...

commands.name: load_assembly
commands.description: edit,long    Load a .NET assembly, a folder, or a native image (PE, ELF, Mach-O, wasm).

commands.name: load_session
commands.description: destructive,long Restore a save_session file: find each file (recorded path, relative path, else SHA-256 under sea...

commands.name: read_result
commands.description: destructive  Page, search or save a kept result (r-..., kept 7 days).

commands.name: reload_assembly
commands.description: destructive  Re-read an assembly from disk (after an update or an overwriting save), discarding unsaved edits.

commands.name: save_session
commands.description: destructive  Save loaded files, .NET edits, native patches, names, comments, notes and open dumps to one JSON...

commands.name: server_status
commands.description: read-only    Server version, program, client, catalog digest, loaded files, limits, capabilities with fixes an...

commands.name: unload_assembly
commands.description: destructive  Remove an assembly (unsaved edits are discarded) or close a dump id.

commands.name: update
commands.description:
Install the latest release (installed copies only) and refresh existing
registrations; it never adds clients.
--version X     install release X instead, also an older one (rollback)
--dry-run       show the release, asset and checksum manifest it would use
